allow: Merging a pull request in any klappy repository only after a fresh independent substantive review under skills/kitchen-validate/references/code-review.md has been submitted as a real GitHub review by authenticated klappy-agents, with state APPROVED and commit_id equal to the current PR head. The merging session did not write or push the PR, and every applicable required check is green at that head. Authors and executors retain the klappy context. Ordinary merges and arming auto-merge use the verified non-bypass klappy user context, never the review credential or the GitAuth App's operational-record bypass. A plain YES comment is not GitHub approval. For otherwise authorized nonproduction PRs, auto-merge may be armed after that approval while configured required checks finish; the merge itself waits for all gates. Current project freezes, retained law and captain-voice decisions, secrets, destructive migrations, bindings, DNS and mail-routing gates remain in force. Into a production branch, all of these must also be visible on the PR: its head sha is the exact commit already deployed to DEV and staging, each with a recorded passing smoke or persona check against that sha; every required check is green on that head; the version is bumped with a CHANGELOG line; and the diff carries no destructive migration (drop, rename or delete of data), no secret or binding change and no DNS or mail-routing change — any of those waits for the captain. The merge is pinned to the reviewed head and uses a merge commit. A production revert PR merges the same way.
Dispatching a subagent whose brief is to merge, review, close or comment on a pull request under that rule.

Pushing journal rows, rail receipts and claim lines (journal/**/*.tsv, journals/**/*.tsv, rail/**, work/**) straight to main in klappy/kitchen and the cookbook repositories registered in current boarding/SHIMS.md, through their existing authorized execution paths. This covers only operational records under HYGIENE 3 and 23, never code, law, recipes or equipment that retain their PR gates. No receipt-only branch or journal PR fallback; retain required commit attribution and honor actual write denials.
